extracted.intended_audience: US patent applicants and practitioners preparing European (EPO) patent claim sets
extracted.subtask_short: EP claim drafting for US applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for converting a US-style claim set into one that complies with European Patent Office (EPO) requirements, covering permitted independent claims, unity of invention, excess-claim fees, use of reference signs, and practical drafting strategies to avoid fees and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: One independent claim per category (Rule 43(2) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application may contain more than one independent claim in the same category (product, process, apparatus or use) only if the subject-matter of the application involves one of the following: (a) a plurality of interrelated products, (b) different uses of a product or apparatus, (c) alternative solutions to a particular problem, where it is inappropriate to cover these alternatives by a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are four categories of independent claims: product, process, apparatus and use. Having more than one independent claim in one category is generally not allowed except for the three situations (a)-(c). See EPO Examination Guidelines (Part F – Chapter IV 3.2) for further detail and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Art. 82 EPC; Rule 44 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The European patent application shall relate to one invention only, or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. A group of inventions fulfils unity only when there is a technical relationship among them involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features (features which define a contribution over the prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination whether inventions form a single general inventive concept is made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim. The EPO uses a detailed procedure for assessing unity (see EPO Examination Guidelines Part F – Chapter V). Unity objections and divisional/partial filing issues arise if this requirement is not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees (Rule 45 EPC; Rules relating to Fees Art. 2(1) No. 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application comprising more than fifteen claims incurs payment of claims fees for the 16th and each subsequent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current amounts (at time of article): €265 per claim for claims 16–50, and €660 per claim above 50. Practical implication: reduce claims to 15 where possible to avoid substantial fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims with reference signs (Rule 43(7) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the European patent application contains drawings including reference signs, the technical features specified in the claims shall preferably be followed by such reference signs relating to these features, placed in parentheses, if the intelligibility of the claim can thereby be increased. These reference signs shall not be construed as limiting the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application has drawings, add corresponding reference numbers to the claims to increase intelligibility, but be aware reference signs are not to be treated as limiting. Practical advice in the article reiterates adding corresponding reference numbers when drawings exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies to reduce claim count (drafting techniques acceptable at the EPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical drafting techniques to conform a US-style claim set to EPO practice and avoid excess-claim fees and objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested measures: reduce the number of claims to 15; use multiple dependencies (allowed at the EPO) to shorten claim lists; combine dependent claims by using wording such as 'preferably', 'optionally', 'in particular'; transfer some claims into the description as 'claim clauses'. These techniques help avoid fees and simplify conformity to EPO expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple independent claims in same category (practical conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If several independent claims exist in the same category, the applicant should select the most important independent claim and rewrite the others as dependent claims or remove them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical recommendation to avoid violating the 'one independent claim per category' principle — converting secondary independent claims into dependencies or deleting them reduces risk of objection under Rule 43(2) EPC.
